rationale: The conditional design is internally coherent and does concentrate both legs among profitable firms so it is an accrual-credibility bet rather than a profitability bet, but it hinges entirely on RANK being a non-negative [0,1] percentile — if RANK is demeaned, unprofitable working-capital builders land in the long leg and the sign flips — and SIGN(ΔWC) discards magnitude in a variable that is close to a coin flip year to year.

This is a single-ingredient numerator swap on the archived ProfitPerAccrualBloat expression, i.e. exactly the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and the resulting quantity is essentially return on net operating assets (RNOA), a long-standing published profitability measure rather than a new cross-theme construct.

The accrual leg is the textbook Sloan (1996) balance-sheet accrual and the profitability leg is standard operating profitability, so the signal is a mechanical equal-weight sum of two of the best-known published anomalies with no genuine interaction — a rank difference is additive, not conditional, so a positive result would teach nothing beyond "both anomalies exist."

Substituting a multi-period trend in the NOA stock for the one-year accrual flow is a defensible slow-moving-accounting-quality state and is the more interesting of the sign-conditioned trio, but it shares the RANK-convention fragility of Signal 1, is structurally the third instance of the same template in this batch, and the NOA-growth conditioner overlaps heavily with the published net-operating-asset/asset-growth anomaly.

The restriction to asset-side accruals is an economically sharper conditioner than aggregate working capital and the sign is correct under the Compustat "decrease (increase)" convention for recch/invch, but the entire result inverts if those fields are stored as raw balance changes, and cash-flow-statement item coverage will likely bind hard on the already-thin sample.

Conditioning profitability on the second moment of the accrual process is the only genuinely distinct lesson in the batch and the accruals-exclusive wcap construction avoids the ib−oancf overlap, though multiplying two non-negative ranks behaves much like an additive composite of two separately-known effects and a 5-period VOL window on annual accruals is a noisy discretion proxy.
